title: Finite commuting squares for the supported diagonal scalar
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an arbitrary scheme S on which l is invertible, a Presentation p and any KernelSplittingData k [def-sp-tower-p1-kernel-scalar-data]. The diagonal is Cartier, and for every positive level n+1 there exist canonical ProjectiveCoordinates c and the ordinary finite unit/Chern splitting bP over P for which KernelFiniteNormalization holds: the specified alpha, pushed delta, trace and composite WordComparison squares, and both ordinary finite diagonal scalar identities. These are finite-level comparisons only; no tower scalar identity or tower splitting base-change square is asserted.

proof.text: The evaluation assertions of [det-sp-tower-classes](3),(4) send $\delta_\bullet$ and $t_i$ to the finite diagonal and splitting trace. The canonical evaluation/composition/mate comparisons of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and [lem-sp-tower-p1-etale-origin-comparisons] identify their composition with $\alpha_i$ with $\nu_P^*(t_{P,B_n}\circ Rp_{i*,B_n}(\delta_{B_n})\circ\alpha_{i,B_n})$. In particular the source is the composition identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$, rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism. The sign is the one in [det-sp-tower-classes](3): precomposition with the divisor unit gives $c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. Thus the finite class is the supported class with the sign required in [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals].

source.place: Levelwise check: identify the specified finite composites

proof.text: For every $n\geq1$ put $N=\ell^n$ and $A=B_n$. Then $N\geq1$, $NA=0$ and $N$ is invertible on $S$. The ring $B_n$ is finite: writing $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ identifies it with $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$, a finite coefficient ring of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All hypotheses of [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals] therefore hold. That node gives both displayed finite composites equal to $1_{(B_n)_P}$ over this arbitrary base. By step 4, $e_n(c_i)=1_{(B_n)_P}$ on the pro-etale site, with the prescribed comparison, for both $i$.

theorem towerP1KernelFiniteComparison (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : IsUnit (l : Γ(S, ⊤))) (p : Presentation l E S hS)
    (k : KernelSplittingData l E p) :
    ∃ hD : (diagonalImmersion S).ker.IsInvertible,
      ∀ n : ℕ, k.finiteNormalization l E hD n
